title: Apollo Says It's Listening, Responding to Data-Center Pushback
source_used: Briefs Finance, relaying a Bloomberg Television interview (7 Oct 2026); Bloomberg is the reporter
key_facts: Olivia Wassenaar, Apollo's global head of infrastructure, said in a Bloomberg Television interview on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026 that Apollo is working to stop local opposition derailing AI infrastructure financing.
She said: 'We listen and respond', and that Apollo wants to put data centres where communities want them.
Pushback is driven by communities' worries about higher utility bills and environmental harm.
Oracle's planned New Mexico data centre campus, Project Jupiter, faced heavy local protests; Oracle invoked force majeure (a contract escape clause) on its obligations.
Wassenaar said Apollo worries more about falling behind on infrastructure investment than about overbuilding, and that natural gas is 'not just a transition fuel'.
Jaycee Pribulsky, Apollo's chief sustainability officer, said the current cost of capital 'really requires creativity in structuring deals'.
Apollo has committed to deploy more than $100 billion by 2030 to back clean-energy projects and the decarbonisation of industry.
quote_evidence: "We listen and respond," she said, adding, "We want to make sure we are putting data centers where folks want data centers to be put."
Apollo has committed to deploy more than $100 billion by 2030 to back clean-energy projects and the decarbonization of industry.
"We will be using natural gas for a long time," she said. "This is not just a transition fuel."
why_it_matters_hint: A major investor says it will keep financing AI data centres and will listen to local objections; the view is the company's own.
